beats.narration_text: Artwork is not collision geometry. A rectangle gives crisp platformer edges; a capsule gives smoother rounded contacts. Resize the shape resource instead of scaling the physics node. Keep collision shapes as direct children of their body.

lecture.why: The spatial or temporal transformation is the claim; a physical-object metaphor would obscure its exact geometry.

beats.narration_text: A static body resists impacts. It can represent a wall or provide conveyor velocity without moving its geometry. A platform following a path belongs on an animatable body, with its movement synchronized to physics.

lecture.why: The spatial or temporal transformation is the claim; a physical-object metaphor would obscure its exact geometry.

beats.narration_text: A rigid body asks the solver to calculate motion. Forces sustain a push; an impulse produces a one-time change. For this isolated example, mass two and impulse one hundred twenty predict a velocity change of sixty.

rb.position=Vector2(380,300)
    rb.mass=2.0
    rb.gravity_scale=0.0
    rb.linear_damp=0.0
    rb.collision_layer=L.bit(L.DEBRIS);rb.collision_mask=L.bit(L.WORLD)
    rb.contact_monitor=true;rb.max_contacts_reported=4
    shape(rb,Vector2(70,70),Color("8b8f96"));stage.add_child(rb)
    await ticks(2)

    await ticks(2)
    check("impulse changes velocity",absf(rb.linear_velocity.x-60)<1,rb.linear_velocity.x)

beats.narration_text: The layer-value methods take one-based layer numbers. Layer three corresponds to bit value four. A raw mask combines bits; the Inspector displays named categories. Keep one constants file synchronized with the project layer names.

lecture.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

props.title: bits · source excerpt
props.code:
static func bit(layer: int) -> int:
    assert(layer >= 1 and layer <= 32)
    return 1 << (layer - 1)

# Also executed: godot/lab.gd:104
    check("layer 3 bit",L.bit(3)==4,L.bit(3))

beats.narration_text: Our coin detected the player even though the player did not scan pickups. Removing the area's mask prevented detection. That is a directed area query. Do not turn it into a universal rule that every body pair needs reciprocal masks.

beats.narration_text: Two nodes can share the same Shape resource. Resize that shared resource and both boundaries change. Duplicate the resource when you need one independent boundary. This is resource ownership, separate from whether the nodes were instanced separately.

lecture.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

props.code:
left.shape = shape
    right.shape = shape
    left.shape.size = Vector2(40,20)
    check("shared resize propagates",right.shape.size.x==40,right.shape.size)
    right.shape = right.shape.duplicate()
    right.shape.size = Vector2(10,20)
    check("duplicate isolates resize",left.shape.size.x==40,left.shape.size)

beats.narration_text: A TileSet owns tile collision polygons and their physics categories. TileMapLayer places cells and builds the bodies. A stateful block is often easier as its own scene; repeated terrain suits tiles. Keep their responsibilities distinct.

beats.narration_text: This collision touched cell three, zero. The body's resource identifier mapped to quadrant zero, zero. Physics chunking groups compatible tile geometry, so the body identifier does not uniquely identify the struck cell. Disabling chunking changes that tradeoff.

beats.narration_text: Probe slightly into the hit surface, against its outward normal. Convert that world point into the tile layer's local coordinates, then map it to a cell. The probe distance is example-specific; test transformed layers and contacts near cell boundaries.

lecture.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

props.title: contact · source excerpt
props.code:
static func cell_at(tiles: TileMapLayer, point: Vector2, normal: Vector2) -> Vector2i:
    # Two pixels is a lab-specific probe distance; tune for tile size and transforms.
    var probe := point - normal * 2.0
    return tiles.local_to_map(tiles.to_local(probe))

beats.narration_text: The checked four point seven shape reference exposes a one-way direction. The default points down in two D coordinates. This is a body collision feature, not an area's overlap policy. Test tilted platforms rather than assuming older tutorial behavior.

beats.narration_text: Separate one-way surfaces onto their own layer, then temporarily stop scanning it. A short physics timer is a simple drop-through policy. Before restoring collision in a real game, ensure the character has cleared the platform and handle overlapping requests.

lecture.why: Exact runnable source is the teaching target; a full editor layout would reduce usable code size.

props.title: drop · source excerpt
props.code:
func drop_through() -> void:
    set_collision_mask_value(Layers.ONE_WAY, false)
    await get_tree().create_timer(0.2, true, true).timeout
    # Minimal timed policy: production code must check that the body is clear.
    set_collision_mask_value(Layers.ONE_WAY, true)

beats.narration_text: For fast rigid bodies, continuous collision detection can reduce tunneling. Two D provides ray and shape modes; three D exposes its own settings. Also consider thicker collision geometry and a higher physics rate. None is a universal prevention guarantee.

beats.narration_text: A missed coin suggests filtering. An offset boundary suggests scale or a shared resource. A wrong tile suggests contact lookup. A slope flicker suggests movement order or snap. Treat each as a hypothesis, then change one variable and rerun.

beats.narration_text: The same responsibilities transfer to three D nodes. Start with boxes, spheres, or capsules. Convex shapes suit movable objects; a few convex pieces can approximate a complex outline. Concave triangle collision is generally for static environments and costs more.

lecture.why: The spatial or temporal transformation is the claim; a physical-object metaphor would obscure its exact geometry.

beats.narration_text: Review generated code against the chosen release. Godot three's kinematic body, instance method, and movement signature differ from Godot four. Check annotation, await, signal connection, scene-change, and one-based collision APIs too. Confident syntax is not evidence.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. For CSYE seventy-two seventy, Building Virtual Environments. Choose geometry and body roles independently of artwork.
